events.title: Ferdinand and Isabella capture Granada
events.summary: The fall of the last Muslim kingdom in Spain ends centuries of campaigns.
events.description: On January 2, 1492, Ferdinand II and Isabella I, the first monarchs of a unified Spain, captured Granada, ending a centuries-long series of military campaigns on the Iberian Peninsula.
events.notificationTitle: The end of an era in Spain
events.notificationBody: In 1492, Ferdinand and Isabella captured Granada.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 2

events.title: Russia surrenders Port Arthur to Japan
events.summary: A major Russian defeat in the Russo-Japanese War.
events.description: On January 2, 1905, during the Russo-Japanese War, Russian forces surrendered Port Arthur (later Lushun, China) to the Japanese.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 2

events.title: NASA's Stardust collects dust from a comet
events.summary: The spacecraft gathers grains from comet Wild 2.
events.description: On January 2, 2004, NASA's Stardust spacecraft collected dust grains from the comet Wild 2.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 2

events.title: The Palmer Raids sweep US cities
events.summary: Thousands are arrested as suspected radicals.
events.description: On January 2, 1920, in the Palmer Raids, thousands of people were arrested in more than 30 US cities, accused of being foreign anarchists, communists, or radical leftists.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 2

events.title: J.R.R. Tolkien is born
events.summary: The author of The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings is born.
events.description: On January 3, 1892, J.R.R. Tolkien, author of The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings, was born.
events.notificationBody: In 1892, J.R.R. Tolkien, author of The Lord of the Rings, was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 3

events.title: Alaska becomes the 49th US state
events.summary: The former territory joins the Union.
events.description: On January 3, 1959, Alaska became the 49th state of the United States.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 3

events.title: China's Chang'e 4 lands on the far side of the Moon
events.summary: It is the first spacecraft to land on the lunar far side.
events.description: On January 3, 2019, China's Chang'e 4 spacecraft, carrying the Yutu-2 rover, landed on the far side of the Moon.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 3

events.title: Pope Leo X excommunicates Martin Luther
events.summary: The break between Luther and Rome becomes formal.
events.description: On January 3, 1521, Pope Leo X excommunicated Martin Luther.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 3

events.title: Washington wins the Battle of Princeton
events.summary: American forces win a battle in New Jersey.
events.description: On January 3, 1777, during the American Revolution, the Battle of Princeton was fought in New Jersey.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 3

events.title: Louis Braille is born
events.summary: The inventor of the raised-dot writing system is born near Paris.
events.description: On January 4, 1809, Louis Braille, who developed the system of printing and writing for the blind that bears his name, was born near Paris.
events.notificationBody: In 1809, Louis Braille, inventor of the braille system, was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 4

events.title: Burma gains independence from Britain
events.summary: The country now called Myanmar becomes independent.
events.description: On January 4, 1948, Burma, today called Myanmar, formally gained independence from Great Britain.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 4

events.title: The Burj Khalifa opens in Dubai
events.summary: The world's tallest building officially opens.
events.description: On January 4, 2010, the Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building, officially opened in Dubai.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 4

events.title: Albert Camus dies in a car accident
events.summary: The novelist and playwright is killed in France.
events.description: On January 4, 1960, the novelist and playwright Albert Camus was killed in an automobile accident in France.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 4

events.title: Solomon Northup regains his freedom
events.summary: A free Black man kidnapped into slavery is legally freed.
events.description: On January 4, 1853, Solomon Northup, a free Black man who had been kidnapped in Washington, D.C., and sold into slavery, legally obtained his freedom.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 4

events.title: Waiting for Godot is staged for the first time
events.summary: Samuel Beckett's play premieres in Paris.
events.description: On January 5, 1953, Samuel Beckett's Waiting for Godot was staged for the first time, in Paris.
events.notificationBody: In 1953, Beckett's Waiting for Godot premiered in Paris.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 5

events.title: Construction begins on the Golden Gate Bridge
events.summary: Work starts on the bridge linking San Francisco and Marin county.
events.description: On January 5, 1933, construction began on the Golden Gate Bridge, which connects San Francisco with Marin county.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 5

events.title: The dwarf planet Eris is discovered
events.summary: Astronomers spot it in images taken two years earlier.
events.description: On January 5, 2005, the dwarf planet Eris was discovered in images taken two years earlier at Palomar Observatory.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 5

events.title: Henry Ford doubles his workers' pay
events.summary: Ford raises daily pay from $2.40 to $5.
events.description: On January 5, 1914, Henry Ford raised his workers' pay from $2.40 to $5.00 a day.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 5

events.title: Nellie Tayloe Ross becomes the first woman US governor
events.summary: She takes office in Wyoming.
events.description: On January 5, 1925, Nellie Tayloe Ross took office in Wyoming, becoming the first woman governor in the United States.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 5

events.title: Franklin D. Roosevelt outlines the Four Freedoms
events.summary: His State of the Union message names four essential freedoms.
events.description: On January 6, 1941, US President Franklin D. Roosevelt outlined his Four Freedoms in his State of the Union message.
events.notificationBody: In 1941, Franklin D. Roosevelt set out his Four Freedoms.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 6

events.title: Henry VIII marries Anne of Cleves
events.summary: She becomes the fourth of his six wives.
events.description: On January 6, 1540, Henry VIII of England married Anne of Cleves, the fourth of his six wives.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 6

events.title: Britain recognizes the People's Republic of China
events.summary: The UK formally recognizes the new Communist government.
events.description: On January 6, 1950, Great Britain announced its recognition of the People's Republic of China.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 6

events.title: Composer Max Bruch is born
events.summary: The Romantic composer is born in Cologne.
events.description: On January 6, 1838, the composer Max Bruch was born in Cologne, in what is today Germany.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 6

events.title: Richard II of England is born
events.summary: The future king will reign from 1377 to 1399.
events.description: On January 6, 1367, the future King Richard II of England was born. He reigned from 1377 to 1399.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 6

events.title: Marian Anderson sings at the Metropolitan Opera
events.summary: The contralto performs with the Met for the first time.
events.description: On January 7, 1955, the American contralto Marian Anderson first performed with the Metropolitan Opera in New York City.
events.notificationTitle: A voice that opened the Met
events.notificationBody: In 1955, Marian Anderson made her Metropolitan Opera debut.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 7

events.title: Vietnamese forces take Phnom Penh
events.summary: The Khmer Rouge regime of Pol Pot is driven from power.
events.description: On January 7, 1979, Vietnamese forces took control of Phnom Penh, Cambodia, removing the Khmer Rouge and Pol Pot from power.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 7

events.title: Surveyor 7 launches toward the Moon
events.summary: The uncrewed probe will make a soft lunar landing.
events.description: On January 7, 1968, the uncrewed US space probe Surveyor 7 was launched; it went on to make a soft landing on the Moon.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 7

events.title: Egypt marks Christmas as a national holiday
events.summary: Coptic Christmas becomes a public holiday for the first time.
events.description: On January 7, 2003, Christmas was celebrated as a national holiday in Egypt for the first time.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 7

events.title: John Kufuor is inaugurated in Ghana
events.summary: Ghana completes its first peaceful transfer of power between governments.
events.description: On January 7, 2001, John Kufuor was inaugurated as president of Ghana in the country's first peaceful transition of government.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 7

events.title: The African National Congress is founded
events.summary: The movement that will lead the struggle against apartheid is born.
events.description: On January 8, 1912, the African National Congress was founded in South Africa.
events.notificationBody: In 1912, the African National Congress was founded in South Africa.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 8

events.title: Woodrow Wilson announces his Fourteen Points
events.summary: The US president sets out his plan for peace after World War I.
events.description: On January 8, 1918, US President Woodrow Wilson announced his Fourteen Points, a program for peace after World War I.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 8

events.title: Charles de Gaulle becomes president of the Fifth Republic
events.summary: France's new constitutional order gets its first president.
events.description: On January 8, 1959, Charles de Gaulle was inaugurated as president of France's Fifth Republic.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 8

events.title: Stephen Hawking is born
events.summary: The physicist known for his work on black holes is born.
events.description: On January 8, 1942, the physicist Stephen Hawking was born. He developed a theory of exploding black holes.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 8

events.title: Elvis Presley is born
events.summary: The future 'King of Rock and Roll' is born.
events.description: On January 8, 1935, Elvis Presley, widely known as the King of Rock and Roll, was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 8
